stem: A strong evaluation of an irrigation project should include:

options.C: Only the number of public speeches
options.D: Water reliability, farm incomes, ecological costs and distribution

option_audit.A: Incorrect: infrastructure length alone omits water delivery, irrigation potential utilised, socio-economic and environmental impacts.
option_audit.B: Incorrect: sanctioned budget is an input, not evidence of benefits or project performance.
option_audit.C: Incorrect: speech counts are not a measure of irrigation performance or benefits.
option_audit.D: Correct: multidimensional evaluation includes water delivery and use efficiency, agro-economic and socio-economic effects, environmental impacts, and distribution among beneficiaries.

primary_sources.finding: Central Water Commission post-project performance evaluation explicitly includes system performance, agro-economic, socio-economic and environmental impacts and economic analysis; water use efficiency studies cover delivery, application and irrigation potential created/utilised.
PMKSY seeks expanded irrigation coverage and improved water use efficiency, with sustainability and groundwater extraction constraints.
Community and stakeholder participation includes women, landless workers and marginalised groups, and evaluation and monitoring of sustainability.

limitations: Primary sources support evaluation dimensions, not any quantified outcome of a specific irrigation project.
Farm-income measurement is a sensible agro-economic indicator but was not shown to be mandatory in every evaluation framework.
No independent reviewer or official PYQ authentication.
This is evidence-only; no master/PDF changes or R1-R8 gate promotion.
